1. The Moon is tidally locked to Earth, meaning the same side always faces our planet, so we never see the "far side" from the ground.

2. The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth at a rate of about 3.8 centimeters per year—roughly the same speed at which fingernails grow.

3. Most scientists believe the Moon formed approximately 4.5 billion years ago when a Mars-sized object named Theia collided with the early Earth, sending debris into orbit that eventually coalesced into the Moon.
